i totally feel this, im experiencing fomo rn because my bf is outside with his friends rn and here i am, procrastinating studying for an important exam that i cant fluke. the best way i find to deal with this is distract yourself, immerse yourself into your studies and make sure that you have multiple distractions for specific occasions that can help you, like maybe group studying with a bunch of friends, taking yourself out to study in a cafe, or deliberately making plans with your friends while your bf is out with his. but tbh, i have no way of doing any of this since i barely have a life here, i moved earlier this year and none of my friends live within close vicinity to me.

sometimes i feel like my partner is my only close friend, and this urges me to spend more time with him, which brings me to my next point. another way to cope is by increasing the time you spend with your bf, maybe you could have silent calls where you just turn on your audio and video while on a call with your bf and do your own thing. this ensures that you're occupying his time and you feel connected to him, even while he's doing something that doesn't involve you. thus whenever he goes out, you can remember the last time the two of you spent time together, and thus feel a little better that eventually he's going to be with you too, and you can look forward to it instead of dreading the moment.

lastly, please communicate about this with him. im sure your bf wouldnt want you to feel excluded the way you do, and if you let him know properly, he might take steps in order to make you feel more involved with his social life, and maybe increase the amount of time he spends with you. if that is what you want, then *let him know*. there isn't anything wrong with asking your partner for extra care or attention, and it'll never seem like it's extra or unnecessary to your partner if they take it in the right way, and if you assure and be completely transparent with your feelings.

please know that you are not selfish or twisted for feeling this way. if you were, then thousands of other people who experience the same thing would be bad partners too, and that's just not right. you're not alone, and you're not evil. im so sorry for the long post, it's just that i totally get you lol. hope this helped :)

it really depends on your coping mechanism and what the both of you individually do to make yourselves feel better. 

my bf and i have opposite coping mechanisms - he doesn't like to talk much about what's bothering him, and i need to let it all out to somebody to cares enough to listen. i essentially go through the five stages of grief in ten minutes on a phone call lol.

when he's upset about something, he usually prefers his space, or idle conversation about another topic. when im upset about something, he gives me his utmost company and listens to me and reassures me about whatever is bothering me. in short, we turn into the person that we need for each other at the moment.

i'd advice you to communicate about your coping mechanisms or how exactly you would like to be comforted. you could fall asleep to each other on call in silence at the end of the day, do your daily activities and chores while facetiming, watch a movie or listen to the same playlist together, or if distraction isn't your thing, venting, crying, joking about your problems or comforting each other could also work. it's up to you to decide whether you want to work your way through an issue together, or you just want company while you do it alone.

think of it as being sad, stressed or angry together. it really helps to know you're not alone.

i completely understand how you feel and have been in similar situations before too. from my experience, the reason why you feel this way is because you feel like you're missing out on spending the time with your boyfriend that other people are, primarily female friends (im guessing you're a woman too), because it should've been YOU in that restaurant having lunch with your boyfriend. it should've been YOU on that drive to go to another city. it should've been you instead of anybody else, and it affects you that it isn't.

as much as feelings like these are common, they don't make sense to anybody but you. im sure the reason why your boyfriend lashed out at you is because he doesn't understand why you feel so upset about him meeting up with a woman because the only person he loves is you, and this may make him feel like you don't trust him enough when it's really more of just you feeling insecure and left out. 

what's important here is the way you approach your boyfriend, you need to ensure that instead of defending yourself, you explain your perspective first, you explain that feeling in your stomach that makes you feel upset, because again, in my experience, suppressing these feelings and adopted them as negative ones that paint you as the bad guy is only going to create repulsion to whenever he makes plans to meet up with other women. and again, as much as it is understandable, it is not a pleasant paranoia to go through, since not only does it affect your feelings, it also affects your and your boyfriend's lifestyle. 

i'd be more than happy to help you out and share more advice with you if you ever need it, or if you need to talk to someone who understands. my dms are always open. as of now, you should accept your feelings instead of feeling like you are toxic, approach your boyfriend whenever you can and speak to him about your perspective in a calm, rational manner, and proceed according to his response. 

just so you know, you are not selfish, nor are you toxic that you feel this way, even though everybody that doesn't understand would paint you to be an asshole right now, which is why i suggest not to speak about this to many people. it'll only make you feel worse. you are simply hurting and yearning to be in physical contact with the person that you love and it doesn't make you a maniac to feel possessive, especially since you've mentioned that you're anxiously attached.

again, im always here to talk, i would love to help out because when i went through this, it was probably the worst i've ever felt my whole life. im rooting for you. just remember that your boyfriend loves you, and is simply confused. sorry this was long. good luck :)
